title: Memory executives expect RAM shortage to continue through 2028
gist: Micron's CEO says memory demand will exceed supply for at least two years, with 2027 HBM largely sold out at higher prices and new 2028 clean rooms ramping slowly; Samsung says HBM will take about 30% of DRAM wafer capacity in 2027, squeezing consumer RAM.

insights.claim: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra expects demand for Micron's memory to exceed available supply for at least the next couple of years, and Samsung executive commentary the same week points the same way.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Supports a multi-year memory upcycle thesis; watch pricing and capex commentary from Micron and Samsung.
insights.quote: Overall, supply-demand environment is only getting tighter
insights.locator: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra expects demand

insights.claim: Micron does not know when its supply will catch up with demand, because larger models, growing context, more concurrency and more enterprise agents keep raising memory content and performance needs.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: AI workload growth, not cyclical inventory, is the driver; track model-size and context-length trends as a demand leading indicator.
insights.locator: Micron doesn't know when its supply will catch up

insights.claim: Seventy-five percent of Micron's memory output for 2027 is already accounted for, and most current sales discussions concern 2028.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Demand is locked in roughly two years ahead, giving unusual earnings visibility for Micron.
insights.locator: Seventy-five percent of Micron's memory output

insights.claim: Micron's 2027 HBM volume is largely sold out, at prices much higher than 2026 prices.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Rising contract prices into 2027 point to margin expansion for HBM suppliers.
insights.quote: a large part of the volume is already sold out for 2027 for HBM, and the prices are much higher than 2026 prices
insights.locator: For 2027, a large part of the volume

insights.claim: Demand for HBM is surpassing demand for Micron's DRAM.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Mix shift toward HBM is the key driver of supplier revenue growth.
insights.locator: demand for HBM is surpassing demand

insights.claim: Micron plans to open new clean rooms for memory manufacturing in 2028, yet the CEO expects supply to stay limited because production ramps only gradually after first wafer output.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: New fabs will not relieve tightness quickly; do not price shortage resolution on fab announcements.
insights.quote: Even after they are built, even after first wafer output, production ramps up only gradually in the clean rooms
insights.locator: Micron plans to open new clean rooms

insights.claim: The shift from HBM3E to a greater mix of HBM4 and 4E, given the trade ratio versus standard DRAM, and smaller per-wafer productivity gains from future node transitions, create headwinds to supply growth.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Structural wafer-efficiency losses cap bit supply growth, supporting prices.
insights.quote: Node transitions of the future give less productivity gain per wafer as well.

insights.claim: Samsung EVP Kim Taewoo said HBM will take almost 30 percent of DRAM manufacturers' wafer capacity in 2027, up from 20 percent this year, per Reuters.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Wafer share shifting to HBM directly tightens commodity DRAM supply.
insights.locator: Mehrotra's statements are supported by comments

insights.claim: Micron's Crucial brand stopped selling RAM to consumers this year, announced in December 2025, as Micron prioritizes larger strategic customers in faster-growing segments.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A major supplier exiting consumer RAM shows data-center memory outranks consumer margins.
insights.locator: This year, Micron's Crucial brand stopped

insights.claim: Capacity prioritizing AI and server memory limits supply for consumer devices, raising costs for prebuilt PCs, pushing OEMs toward lower RAM configurations at higher prices, and lifting prices of smartphones, streaming sticks and gaming consoles.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Device makers face margin and unit-demand pressure; consumer hardware names are exposed to memory input costs.
insights.locator: Consumers have already felt the memory crunch
